Decision Table for the BOIN-ET Design

Source: R/boin_et_decision_table.R
boin_et_decision_table.Rd

Tabulate the decision of the BOIN-ET design for every number of DLTs and responses at the current dose, for the given numbers of patients, in the form of Table 2 of Takeda, Taguri and Morita (2018). The table also marks the counts for which the dose is no longer admissible.

Usage

boin_et_decision_table(
  target,
  target_resp,
  n = c(3, 6, 9, 12),
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  p_saf_resp = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.99,
  p_eli = NULL,
  p_eli_resp = NULL,
  prior = rep(1/6, 6)
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Target DLT probability, for example 0.30.

target_resp

Numeric scalar. Target response probability, for example 0.60.

n

Integer vector. Numbers of patients at the current dose to tabulate. Defaults to c(3, 6, 9, 12).

p_saf

Numeric scalar. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.1 * target, the value recommended by Takeda et al. (2018), which is far below the 0.6 * target of the BOIN design.

p_tox

Numeric scalar. Lowest DLT probability deemed overly toxic. Defaults to 1.4 * target.

p_saf_resp

Numeric scalar. Highest response probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.6 * target_resp.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A dose is no longer admissible when the posterior probability that its DLT rate is below p_eli falls below 1 - cutoff_eli. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. A dose is no longer admissible when the posterior probability that its response rate is above p_eli_resp falls below 1 - cutoff_eli_resp. Defaults to 0.99.

p_eli

Numeric scalar or NULL. DLT probability of the rule above. Defaults to NULL, which uses target as the 'boinet' package does. Takeda et al. (2018) used 0.40 with a cutoff of 0.90.

p_eli_resp

Numeric scalar or NULL. Response probability of the rule above. Defaults to NULL, which uses p_saf_resp as the 'boinet' package does. Takeda et al. (2018) used 0.20 with a cutoff of 0.90.

prior

Numeric vector of length 6. Prior probabilities of the six hypotheses. Defaults to rep(1 / 6, 6), the noninformative choice of the article. The third hypothesis, under which every decision is correct, does not enter the criterion.

Value

An object of class boin_et_decision_table, which is a data frame with one row per combination of n patients, n_tox DLTs and n_resp responses, and the columns

n, n_tox, n_resp

The counts.

decision

"E" to escalate, "S" to stay, "D" to de-escalate and "E/S/D" when the next dose is chosen among the current dose and its neighbors by their observed response rates.

tox_excluded, resp_excluded

Whether the DLT data or the response data make the dose inadmissible.

The boundaries are attached as the attribute "boundary", an object of class boin_et_boundary.

Details

When the observed DLT rate is at most lambda1 and the observed response rate at most eta1, the dose is escalated; when the DLT rate is below lambda2 and the response rate above eta1, the next cohort stays; when the DLT rate is at least lambda2, the dose is de-escalated. Otherwise the dose is escalated when the next dose has not been tried, and the next cohort goes to the dose with the highest observed response rate among the current dose and its neighbors, with ties broken at random. An inadmissible dose is skipped by boin_et_simulate.

References

Takeda, K., Taguri, M. and Morita, S. (2018). BOIN-ET: Bayesian optimal interval design for dose finding based on both efficacy and toxicity outcomes. Pharmaceutical Statistics, 17(4), 383-395. doi:10.1002/pst.1864

See also

boin_et_boundary, boin_et_simulate

Examples

# Table 2 of Takeda et al. (2018)
tab <- boin_et_decision_table(target = 0.30, target_resp = 0.60, n = c(3, 6))
tab
#> BOIN-ET decision table
#>   lambda1 = 0.14, lambda2 = 0.35, eta1 = 0.48
#> 
#> 3 patients
#>     Responses
#> DLTs 0     1     2  3 
#>    0 E     E     S  S 
#>    1 E/S/D E/S/D S  S 
#>    2 D     D     D  D 
#>    3 D*    D*    D* D*
#> 
#> 6 patients
#>     Responses
#> DLTs 0     1     2     3  4  5  6 
#>    0 E     E     E     S  S  S  S 
#>    1 E/S/D E/S/D E/S/D S  S  S  S 
#>    2 E/S/D E/S/D E/S/D S  S  S  S 
#>    3 D     D     D     D  D  D  D 
#>    4 D*    D*    D*    D* D* D* D*
#>    5 D*    D*    D*    D* D* D* D*
#>    6 D*    D*    D*    D* D* D* D*
#> 
#> E = escalate, S = stay, D = de-escalate, E/S/D = choose among the current and neighboring doses;
#> * = the dose is no longer admissible

head(as.data.frame(tab))
#>   n n_tox n_resp decision tox_excluded resp_excluded
#> 1 3     0      0        E        FALSE         FALSE
#> 2 3     0      1        E        FALSE         FALSE
#> 3 3     0      2        S        FALSE         FALSE
#> 4 3     0      3        S        FALSE         FALSE
#> 5 3     1      0    E/S/D        FALSE         FALSE
#> 6 3     1      1    E/S/D        FALSE         FALSE
